test: Rendered multiplayer room, telemetry, phone voice and reconnect integration
checks: Separate rider browser contexts boot with synthetic live bike telemetry
Host creates a private room with a shareable code
Two named riders share one lobby
Guest cannot start the host race
Phone companion pairs through the rendered code form
Both riders reach the race HUD in the same live room
Authoritative HUD power matches each independent bike fixture
Both clients display live multiplayer and eight-rider standings
Synthetic native voice requires no online speech consent
Voice starts on the synthetic offline bridge
Phone voice controls only its paired rider on the real server
Synthetic phone voice steers the authoritative multiplayer rider
Duplicate final voice result is not replayed on the server
Reloading the phone restores pairing without a new code
Restored phone sequence accepts the next real control command
Reload/rejoin retains rider identity and immediately accepted power input
Leaving removes the guest and does not reopen the race HUD
A failed leave POST still stops the race stream and stays home
No uncaught JavaScript errors across rider and phone contexts
limitations: Real Chromium contexts and the actual HTTP/SSE server were used.
Peloton telemetry and native speech results were synthetic fixtures; no physical bike or microphone was used.
This does not certify Android installation, real speech recognition, remote HTTPS hosting, or internet latency.
